summary: Backtracking = build a partial solution, recurse, then UNDO the choice before trying the next. It powers permutations, subsets, parentheses, phone-letter combos, and grid maze paths. Two ideas cover most of it: the choose/explore/unchoose template, and grid DFS with a visited marker that you restore on the way out. A few problems (Kth Symbol) are pure divide-and-conquer recurrences, not search.

thoughtProcess.title: Write the recursion as choose -> explore -> unchoose.
thoughtProcess.body: Add a choice to the current path, recurse, then remove it. The 'remove it' line is the one people forget; without it the path leaks state into sibling branches.

thoughtProcess.title: Subsets vs permutations vs combinations — the shape of the recursion differs.
thoughtProcess.body: Subsets: at each index, include or skip. Permutations: pick any unused element (track used[]). Combinations/parentheses: constrain choices (e.g. can add ')' only if open>close).

thoughtProcess.title: Grid/maze paths: DFS with visited + restore, and prune at the borders.
thoughtProcess.body: Mark cell visited before recursing into neighbours, unmark after. Check bounds and hurdles before stepping. For shortest path in an unweighted grid prefer BFS over backtracking.

keyPatterns.name: Backtracking template
keyPatterns.template:
void go(path, choices):
  if complete: record(path); return
  for c in choices:
    path.add(c)          // choose
    go(path, next)       // explore
    path.removeLast()    // UNCHOOSE

keyPatterns.name: Grid DFS with restore
keyPatterns.when: Count/print paths through a maze with obstacles
keyPatterns.template: dfs(r,c): if out/hurdle/visited return; visit; recurse 4 dirs; unvisit
examples: General maze / island grid DFS (mark visited, unmark on return). The Section 3 maze problems here use simpler variants: 1D recursion (Staircase), Down/Right only (Print All Maze Paths), or BFS (Shortest Path in Binary Maze).

keyPatterns.name: Divide-and-conquer recurrence
keyPatterns.when: Kth element of a self-similar sequence
keyPatterns.template: Kth-symbol: value(n,k) depends on value(n-1, k/2) and a flip

commonMistakes.title: Forgetting to undo the choice
commonMistakes.why: State leaks into sibling branches, producing wrong/duplicated results.

commonMistakes.title: Not restoring visited in grid DFS
commonMistakes.why: A cell blocked on one path stays blocked for all other paths, undercounting solutions.

edgeCases: Empty input (empty string / empty set) — the base case should still record the single empty solution where appropriate.
Duplicates in the input for subsets/permutations — sort and skip equal siblings to avoid repeat results.
Recursion depth grows with input size; deep grids/strings can approach the stack limit.
Shortest-path in an unweighted grid: BFS gives the true minimum; DFS/backtracking can explore exponentially.
